bullets.title: META cloud compute pivot triggers AI capex debate; CRWV/NBIS -13-17% on competition fears
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported META building 'Meta Compute' cloud business to sell excess AI infrastructure capacity, sparking a sector-wide debate. JPM, Citi, Morgan Stanley, and others view it as optionality that adds ~$3 EPS in '28 (every 250 MW leased at $40/Watt), while bears cite it as evidence of AI ROI failure; META rose ~9% on the news while neoclouds CRWV (-13%) and NBIS (-17%) collapsed on fears META becomes a direct competitor. Citi reiterates Buy/$850, JPM downgraded META to Neutral with $725 PT (from OW in April).

bullets.title: MU/SNDK: UBS raises memory price targets sharply; MU PT $1,625 on DRAM undersupply through 2028
bullets.body: UBS raised 2H26 DDR contract pricing forecasts to +32% QoQ in 3Q and +18% in 4Q (vs prior +17%/+12%), and NAND to +30% QoQ in 3Q. DRAM industry seen undersupplied until at least 2Q28 with 2027 demand growth (+36.2% YoY) far exceeding supply (+19.3%). MU Buy rated at $1,625 PT; KeyBanc has $1,600 PT. Memory stocks pulled back ~17% from June peak but viewed as temporary.

bullets.title: CMCSA +22% on NBCU/Sky spinoff plan; CHTR +22% on SpaceX mobile talks
bullets.body: Comcast announced a tax-free spin of NBCUniversal and Sky (~1 year timeline); Mike Cavanagh to lead NBCUniversal, Michael Angelakis to lead Comcast cable. Wolfe Research says the breakup likely won't complete and cable/NBCU will merge with peers (Charter/Netflix most likely). CHTR surged on reports of executive-level talks with SpaceX on a consumer mobile phone offering. Citi rates both Buy; CMCSA also upgraded to Buy at Deutsche Bank ($32 PT) and Rosenblatt ($31 PT).

bullets.title: FOXA upgraded to Outperform at Wolfe ($71 PT) on ROKU deal; 36% upside from excessive selloff
bullets.body: Wolfe upgraded FOXA to Outperform with $71 PT, noting the ~23% post-deal decline is an overreaction to the $22B Roku acquisition. Pro forma FOXA trades at 11.8x NTM UFCF with $400M cost synergies; deal shifts narrative from linear TV to multi-channel CTV/streaming with ~45% engagement from streaming. SOTP analysis implies $80/share fair value.

bullets.title: PLTR upgraded to Buy at DA Davidson ($175 PT) on valuation and AI orchestration moat
bullets.body: DA Davidson upgraded PLTR from Neutral to Buy, raising PT to $175 from $165. Analyst Gil Luria notes PLTR is growing 2x faster than peers at a de-rated valuation (down from 200x to 50x forward P/E), with FCF margins that doubled last year and should double again. PLTR-NVDA deal addresses Frontier Labs concerns.

bullets.title: ADBE upgraded to Buy at HSBC ($308 PT); AI disruption fears seen as overdone
bullets.body: HSBC analyst Stephen Bersey upgraded ADBE from Hold to Buy, raising PT to $308 from $282 (46% upside from ~$211). Thesis: no evidence of market share loss, AI disruption fears overblown. ADBE stock is down ~25-30% YTD.

bullets.title: CRM and NOW upgraded to Buy at Guggenheim; AI bear case called 'hallucination'
bullets.body: Guggenheim upgraded CRM to Buy with $228 PT (46% upside from ~$157) and NOW to Buy with $125 PT (26% upside from ~$99), both from Neutral. Analyst John DiFucci argues AI will materially impact software but most names will persist; valuations imply perpetual decline that is unlikely. Expects subscription revenue growth stabilization in 2026 with acceleration into 2027.

bullets.title: HOOD surges 19.8% on perpetual futures launch; Mizuho raises PT to $130 on global brokerage thesis
bullets.body: Robinhood launched perpetual futures on real-world assets in Europe (gold, silver, oil, FX, ETFs) with up to 10x leverage via Bitstamp, and unveiled Robinhood Chain (L2 blockchain on Arbitrum) with DeFi primitives. June MTD equity, options, and event contract volumes on track for records. Mizuho raised PT from $115 to $130; Piper reiterates OW at $135 PT. KeyBanc views HOOD as potential 'AWS of online brokerages.'

bullets.title: TSLA Q2 deliveries 480K, beat ~406K consensus; +25% YoY
bullets.body: Tesla reported Q2 deliveries of ~480K vehicles (+25% YoY, best growth since 3Q23 per MS), beating a ~397-406K consensus. Energy storage was in-line at 13.5 GWh (+34% YoY). US June auto sales showed Tesla at ~37K units (-27% YoY in US specifically), but global numbers beat. MS raised TSLA estimates on the delivery beat.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $415 on 9GW 2028 capacity; Google Cloud to $300B+ revenue
bullets.body: MS analyst Brian Nowak raised GOOGL PT from $375 to $415, modeling 9 GW of incremental compute capacity in 2028 with 4 GW sold as TPU on 1P basis. Google Cloud revenue projected at $214B/$308B in 2027/2028 (106%/44% growth). 2027/2028 capex raised to $350B/$375B. Stock trading at 18x 2028 EPS vs 21x LT average. GOOGL also saw its €4.13B ($4.7B) EU antitrust fine upheld by the ECJ.

bullets.title: AAPL cuts iPhone 17 production ~15%; seeking White House approval to source chips from Chinese CXMT/YMTC
bullets.body: Apple reduced iPhone 17 production plans amid lower shipment forecasts. Simultaneously, Apple is negotiating to buy memory from Chinese suppliers CXMT and YMTC (both Pentagon-blacklisted) to manage soaring memory costs, while lobbying the White House for political cover. Apple also raised MacBook/iPad prices 15-25% due to memory cost pressure. AAPL also held 'constructive talks' with EU on resolving Siri AI launch disputes.

bullets.title: BE expands Brookfield AI infrastructure partnership 5x to $25B; MS upgrades to OW at $310 PT
bullets.body: Bloom Energy expanded its Brookfield AI infrastructure partnership from $5B to $25B (5 GW capacity framework), up from the original 1 GW deal. Morgan Stanley upgraded BE to Overweight with a $310 PT, noting BE has ~2.5 GW of project wins with AEP, ORCL, and NBIS to date. UBS reiterated Buy, raised TP to $355.

bullets.title: DLR acquires Blackstone's Northern Virginia data centers for $7.8B; 80-330bps FFO accretion
bullets.body: Digital Realty announced acquisition of Blackstone's 64% interest in three fully-leased NOVA data centers (288 MW) at $7.8B gross value ($3.5B to BX via $1.2B cash + $2.3B DLR stock). Initial cap rate >6.5% with 3.6% annual escalator; unlevered return >10%. Expected to be ~80bps accretive to Core FFOPS in 2027 and ~330bps in 2028. Citi maintains Buy with $226 PT.

bullets.title: SMCI -8% on Taiwan office raid over Nvidia chip smuggling investigation
bullets.body: Taiwanese authorities raided Super Micro Computer's offices as part of an expanded investigation into alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips into China. SMCI shares fell ~8% on the news; DELL and HPE gained on competitive displacement expectations. The investigation adds to SMCI's brand and regulatory risk.

bullets.title: VZ -5%+ on $700-800M Q2 loss from BT JV; forms 50:50 international operations venture
bullets.body: Verizon announced a 50:50 JV with BT Group for international operations (~$4B combined revenue, 3,000+ customers in 180+ countries). VZ will pay BT $625M equalization payment and will record $700-800M loss in Q2 from held-for-sale reclassification plus $350-450M severance and $200-300M asset rationalization charges. VZ and T both pressured on the week by Starlink mobile competition fears.

bullets.title: AFRM: Citi raises PT to $115; FY29 GAAP EPS upside scenario of $5.00 (vs consensus $3.72)
bullets.body: Citi reiterated Buy on AFRM and raised PT from $100 to $115, citing growing conviction in growth and profitability. FY29 GAAP EPS could reach $5.00 vs $3.72 consensus in upside scenario driven by 30% GMV growth (new merchants: Intuit, Lowe's, Costco), RLTC margin at 4%+, and GAAP operating margin at 30%. Piper Sandler also initiated AFRM at Overweight.

bullets.title: UBER ends Waymo Phoenix partnership; TSLA FSD advancing in EU
bullets.body: Uber and Waymo terminated their autonomous ride-hailing partnership in Phoenix after nearly 3 years; partnership continues in Austin and Atlanta. Uber is seeking a separate AV partner for Phoenix. Tesla FSD V14 Lite rolled out for older HW3 vehicles; supervised self-driving may reach EU as early as 2028 (Finland regulatory pathway noted).

bullets.title: MSFT planning <2.5% workforce cuts; MSFT 6-month IV at 5-year high of 37 creates call spread opportunity
bullets.body: Microsoft announced job cuts affecting <2.5% of its 220K workforce (~5,500 roles) across sales, consulting, and Xbox divisions, with Xbox margins having fallen to ~3%. Separately, 22V Research recommended costless 1x2 call spreads on MSFT (buy Jan 410 calls / sell Jan 470 calls) as 6-month implied vol jumped from 22 to 37 (5-year high) following MSFT's ~17-18% June decline.

bullets.title: NVDA revenue-sharing model for AI cloud providers; new 'usage-linked earnings' via DSX AI factories
bullets.body: NVIDIA launched a new business model partnering with AI cloud providers through revenue-sharing and credit-support arrangements, enabling scaled deployment of Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs. Sharon AI is deploying up to 40,000 GB300 GPUs; Firmus building 360 MW DSX AI factory in Indonesia with up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs. NVDA also partnered with PLTR on Nemotron open AI model deployment in sovereign environments.

bullets.title: DKNG: 2Q EBITDA estimate cut to $222M (from $265M) on Predictions marketing; Buy/$30 PT maintained
bullets.body: Citi lowered DKNG 2Q adj EBITDA to $222M from $265M due to DraftKings Predictions marketing spend being pulled forward from H2 into Q2. FY adj EBITDA estimate of $787M remains ahead of Street's $767M. DraftKings also launched DKeX proprietary prediction markets exchange with ~$3.4B annualized consumer volume. Citi maintains Buy at $30 PT.
